Anatomic Site:Tumor- FS
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 42-year-old man with a history of oligoastrocytoma
WHO II diagnosed two years ago, now presenting with a recurrence in the right parietal lobe.
Gross Description:
Part A is received fresh from OR6 labeled with the patient's name, medical
record number, and "tumor - FS." It consists of three unoriented, irregularly shaped, soft,
pale gray fragments of brain tissue measuring 1.0 x 0.8 x 0.5 cm,
0.9 x 0.6 x 0.5 cm, and 0.6 x 0.5 x 0.4 cm. A portion of each fragment is
submitted for cytologic preparation, with the remaining tissue submitted in
cassette A1 for permanent section.
Diagnosis Comments:
Immunohistochemical studies reveal negative IDH1-R132H mutation, suggesting
wild-type IDH status. MIB-1 labeling index is elevated, consistent with a high proliferative index.
The tumor shows mixed oligodendroglial and astrocytic components with evidence
of focal microvascular proliferation. No necrosis is identified.
The final diagnosis was communicated to Dr. Elman by phone on 8/15/23.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1 (A) Brain, right parietal lobe, biopsy: Oligoastrocytoma WHO grade II with
features of progression. No definitive necrosis observed.
Defer to permanent section. (Dr. Andrea M. Russo)
Final Diagnosis:
Brain, right parietal lobe, biopsy: Anaplastic oligoastrocytoma with astrocytic
predominance, WHO grade III; see comment.
++++++++++Addendum++++++++++
RESULTED BY 41258 Russo, Andrea
Addendum Comment:
The IDH1-R132H negative status was confirmed with a second immunohistochemical
stain, corroborating the initial findings. The clinical significance of this wild-type status should be considered in treatment planning.

Anatomic Site: Tumor- FS
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 29-year-old woman with a newly diagnosed left temporal lobe tumor.
Initial imaging suggested a low-grade glioma.
Gross Description:
Part A consists of two unoriented, soft, tan-gray fragments of brain tissue
measuring 0.9 x 0.7 x 0.4 cm and 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.3 cm.
Tissue is submitted in cassette A1 for permanent section.
Diagnosis Comments:
Histologic sections reveal a biphasic tumor with both oligodendroglial and astrocytic features.
The tumor shows a low MIB-1 proliferative index and is GFAP positive, indicating
astrocytic differentiation. No microvascular proliferation or necrosis is observed.
These findings were discussed with Dr. Lin via email on 10/11/23.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1 (A) Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Oligodendroglioma with astrocytic
components, WHO grade II. No high-grade features.
Final Diagnosis:
Brain, left temporal lobe, biopsy: Oligoastrocytoma, WHO grade II; see comment.
++++++++++Addendum++++++++++
RESULTED BY 39217 Lin, Emily
Addendum Comment:
Additional staining confirmed the absence of 1p/19q codeletion, supporting the mixed oligoastrocytic nature of the tumor.

Anatomic Site:NP Consult with blocks; Stanford runs add'l stains
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 55-year-old woman with a history of a right occipital brain tumor,
originally diagnosed as an oligoastrocytoma WHO grade II. Recent MRI suggests progression.
Gross Description:
Received are the following materials from outside:
Slides: Six glass slides labeled 'RS-03-22654 H&E SMITH,ANNE Stanford, CA.'
Individual slides bear labels 'C1-1,' 'C2-1,' 'C3-1,' 'C4-1,' 'D1-1,' 'D2-1.'
Blocks: Four paraffin blocks labeled 'RS-03-22654.' Individual blocks bear
labels 'C1,' 'C2,' 'C3,' 'D1.'
Tissue: None.
Hospital or lab: Stanford Medical Center, Stanford, CA.
Pathology report dated: 09/18/2023. This report bears both the patient's name
and 'RS-03-22654.'
Prepared by: Sarah Young, M.D.
Diagnosis Comments:
Sections reveal a recurrent oligoastrocytoma with increased cellularity and
mitotic activity. Foci of microvascular proliferation are noted, consistent with
anaplastic transformation. No necrosis is observed.
Previous FISH analysis reported no 1p/19q codeletion.
The findings were relayed to Dr. Young on 9/25/23.
Final Diagnosis:
Review of outside slides from Stanford Medical Center, Stanford, CA (RS-03-22654):
Brain, biopsy: Anaplastic oligoastrocytoma (WHO Grade III); see comment.
